newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Roccade sale hit by software snag - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Roccade sale hit by software snag - paper.

text.p: The sale price of Dutch state-owned payroll processor Roccade is likely to be lower than expected due to problems over the launch of a new software product, newspaper Het Financieele Dagblad said on Saturday.

No date has yet been set for the privatisation of Roccade Informatica Groep, which has attracted the attention of U.S. computer giant Electronic Data Systems, but the government has said it planned the sale before the end of the year.
The paper said Roccade had run into difficulty over a new salary administration software package for the private market and had to write off 15 million guilders in development costs.
"Roccade was unable to find any buyers for its error-filled 'Pecunia' programme," Het Financieele Dagblad said, adding the product had now been taken off the market.

The additional costs pushed the company's 1996 first half operating profit down to 10.1 million guilders from 14.3 million in 1995, it said. Competition was also hotting up from computer firm Raet, which Roccade jointly owns with Getronics.

Getronics has also made an offer for the whole of Roccade but Het Financieele Dagblad said the government has delayed the privatisation because other parties including EDS have offered -- David Evans, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
